The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are set to be unveiled next month with an all-new A20 Pro chip; a reputable leaker this weekend shared the expected performance gains based on supply chain information.

A20 Pro chip tipped to be 18% faster with 30% improved efficiency

Apple will introduce its latest chip, the A20 Pro, at its big September event.

The A20 Pro will be Apple's first chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process, and rumors also point to a new Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging technology.

Due to all these changes, expectations have been high that this year's chip upgrade will be larger than usual.

Weibo leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" posted this weekend, claiming that according to supply chain information, the A20 Pro will deliver the following gains over the A19 Pro:

  • 18% performance improvement
  • 30% efficiency improvement

The details behind these numbers will undoubtedly become more granular when Apple officially announces them next month. Apple has historically broken down gains by CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine individually.

But if these numbers hold true, the gains are quite substantial. The efficiency improvements should translate to better battery life, while performance will also get a nice boost.

Combined with the speed improvements of iOS 27 itself, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are shaping up to be a notable performance upgrade.

What do you think of the rumored A20 Pro upgrades? Let us know in the comments.
